title: Influencing the Arc of Peoples Lives Without Knowing It
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article reflects on how the everyday choices leaders, coaches, teachers, and parents make can have outsized, long-term effects on the people they lead — effects that often go unrecognized until decades later. It argues that because this influence is largely invisible in the moment, most leaders rarely pause to consider its weight, yet doing so occasionally can sharpen how they show up day to day. The piece closes by citing sociologist William Bruce Cameron's line that not everything that counts can be counted, urging leaders to let every day add up to something meaningful without keeping score.
points: Leaders, coaches, teachers, and parents often shape the long-term arc of others' lives through small, largely unnoticed actions.
The impact of these actions is usually unknown to the leader at the time and only recognized by the affected person years later.
Because this influence is invisible in the moment, most leaders rarely reflect on it, though doing so occasionally is valuable.
Leaders who remember their outsized potential impact tend to make better choices in ordinary moments.
The piece closes with sociologist William Bruce Cameron's reminder that many things that truly count cannot be counted.
quotes: The power of leadership to influence the course of others’ lives goes far beyond enhancing job satisfaction and shaping careers.
Unnoticed at the time and typically unknown until decades later, some of the choices leaders make in the course of an average day can profoundly impact the very arc of people’s lives.
Contemplating the potential impact of their words, actions, and decisions —and the tremendous responsibility that entails — can be humbling for leaders.
Leaders who remember the powerful influence they wield often make better choices in the moment.
Many of the things you can count, don’t count. Many of the things you can’t count, really count.
